songInfo.title: Voodoo Child (Slight Return)
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: E Minor Pentatonic and Blues Scale with Mixolydian 3rds and Dorian 6ths

scalesUsed.name: E Blues Scale
scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - Bb - B - D
scalesUsed.application: Aggressive vocal-like solo lines and crying bends featuring the flat-5 blue note (Bb)

scalesUsed.name: E Minor Pentatonic
scalesUsed.application: Core foundation of the legendary main riff and rhythm accompaniment

scalesUsed.name: E Mixolydian
scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: Major 3rd (G#) and 6th (C#) passing tones over the E7#9 Hendrix chord

mainProgression.description: Unstoppable blues-rock vamp based on a low E pedal drone, punctuated by biting G and A transition chords

sectionProgressions.description: Percussive muted wah-wah strums that gradually build rhythmic momentum into open E octave slaps
Heavy blues-rock groove combining low E single-note bends with the signature dominant 7#9 chord

sectionProgressions.progression: E7 vamp with dynamic octave/fuzz bursts
sectionProgressions.description: Open-ended solo vehicle driven by Mitchell's syncopated drumming and Redding's walking bassline

harmonicFunction: E7#9 (I7#9) - The definitive Hendrix tonic chord combining both major 3rd (G#) and augmented 9th (G natural) for raw blues tension
G (bIII) - Borrowed modal step providing a punchy blues turnaround lift
A (IV) - Subdominant resolution sliding smoothly back down into the open E pedal point
E Open Drone (I) - Ringing low E string creating an earth-shaking resonant acoustic foundation

techniques.name: Wah-Wah Pedal Sweep & Percussive Muting
techniques.description: Synchronizing right-hand 16th-note muted strumming with smooth rocking of the wah pedal treadle to create a human vocal timbre

notes: Fret hand lightly mutes strings across all 6 strings without depressing to frets
Rock foot from heel (bass sweep) to toe (treble sweep) in steady quarter or eighth-note rhythms
Accentuate beat 1 by digging harder with the pick
Produces the iconic 'wacka-chicka' intro sound
sequence: Strum muted strings in alternate picking motion
Open treadle forward on downbeats to filter treble frequencies
Rock heel back on upbeats for throaty low-mid resonance
tips: Keep picking wrist loose and relaxed like a funk rhythm guitarist
Control amp volume to prevent runaway squeal while sweeping

techniques.name: The 'Hendrix Chord' (E7#9) Grip
techniques.description: Fretting the 7#9 chord using a 4-finger shape on the middle strings: Root (7th fret A), Major 3rd (6th fret D), Dominant 7th (7th fret G), and Augmented 9th (8th fret B)

notes: Finger 1: 6th fret D string (G#)
Finger 2: 7th fret A string (E)
Finger 3: 7th fret G string (D)
Finger 4: 8th fret B string (G natural)
sequence: Strike open low E string as bass pedal
Grip middle 4 strings and strike firmly
Apply gentle vibrato to the entire chord shape
Slide down two frets for dynamic turnaround effect
tips: Mute high E string with index finger slant if not sounding
Let low E ring out underneath the upper voicing

techniques.name: Aggressive Unison & Microtonal Blues Bending
techniques.description: Executing wide whole-step and 1.5-step string bends on the G and B strings with rapid vibrato at the peak of the bend

notes: Use ring finger reinforced by middle and index fingers for bending power
Bend 14th fret G string up to pitch while fretting 12th fret B string for screaming unison notes
Control pitch accurately to create expressive vocal cries
sequence: Pluck target note firmly near the bridge pickup
Push string upward using wrist rotation, not finger extension
Add wide, pulsating vibrato once target pitch is locked
tips: Half-step down tuning reduces string tension, facilitating easier multi-step bends
Keep thumb anchored over neck for leverage

sections.name: Wah-Wah Percussive Intro
sections.description: The immortal intro begins with percussive muted rakes through a Vox wah pedal before breaking into open string snaps
notes: Mute strings lightly across the 7th fret without pressing down to the wire
Rock the wah pedal steadily in time with Mitchell's hi-hat count
Let the open low E string ring out as the riff builds explosive intensity

sections.name: Main Riff
sections.description: Full band explosion where Jimi establishes the iconic riff with heavy thumb-over low notes and snappy double stops
notes: Slightly bend the 3rd fret on the low E string up a microtone (blues curl) before resolving to open E
Slap the E7#9 chord on the upbeat of beat 2
Accentuate the dynamic swing feel of the rhythm section

sections.name: Verse 1 Groove
sections.description: Hendrix sings while interweaving blues licks, thumb chords, and wah swells between vocal lines
notes: Leave space for vocals by rolling back guitar volume to around 7
Punctuate vocal lines with stinging pentatonic fills in the 12th position
Use the wah pedal to vocalize responses to your singing

sections.name: Guitar Solo Climax
sections.description: A scorching clinic in high-energy fuzz and octave soloing, featuring screeching overbends and dive-bomb tremolo vibrato
notes: Engage Fuzz Face and Octavia for harmonic-rich octave screaming highs
Use pick hand palm to damp unplayed lower strings during furious high-register runs
Dig deep with wide, expressive vibrato at the 15th and 17th frets

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (SSS Single Coils, Maple or Rosewood neck)
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup for warm throaty blues; Bridge pickup with Fuzz Face for soaring solos

amp.recommended: Marshall 100W Super Lead Plexi (1959 / JTM45/100) running through 4x12 Celestion Greenback cabinets
alternatives: Fender Twin Reverb (for clean pedal platform)

effects.distortion: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (Germanium or Silicon NKT275 / BC108)
effects.reverb: Natural room acoustics or subtle vintage spring reverb
effects.other: Vox V846 Wah-Wah, Roger Mayer Octavia, Shin-ei Uni-Vibe

beginner.title: Rhythm Foundation & The Hendrix Chord
steps: Tune your guitar down one half-step to Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb
Master the E7#9 chord grip (7th fret A, 6th fret D, 7th fret G, 8th fret B)
Practice transitioning smoothly between the open low E string and the E7#9 chord
Learn the G5 (3rd fret) and A5 (5th fret) power chord shifts
beginner.goals: Play the main verse rhythm cleanly in time with a metronome at 80 BPM

intermediate.title: Wah-Wah Synchronization & Riff Dynamics
steps: Coordinate your picking hand muted scratching with the heel-toe motion of a wah-wah pedal
Integrate low E microtonal quarter-step curls on the 3rd fret into the main riff
Learn the Box 1 E Minor Pentatonic scale in the 12th position (frets 12-15)
Practice executing 1-step unison bends on the B and G strings
intermediate.goals: Play the complete intro, verse, and rhythm fills with authentic groove and tone

advanced.title: Complete Solo Transcription & Microtonal Articulation
steps: Master Kirk Hammett and Stevie Ray Vaughan's interpretations alongside Hendrix's original recording
Incorporate intense, wide blues vibrato without slipping out of pitch
Use guitar volume knob dynamically (7 for rhythm chime, 10 for fuzz solo saturation)
Improvise fluently using E Blues and E Mixolydian across the entire neck
advanced.goals: Perform the entire 5-minute song note-for-note including high-register solo climaxes

commonMistakes: Pressing too hard during the muted wah-wah intro, causing unwanted pitched fret notes to ring out
Rushing the tempo: the groove is deep, relaxed, and laid-back at 84 BPM, not rushed
Muting the high E or B string accidentally during the E7#9 chord grip
Bending out of tune on the 1.5-step overbends in the solo section
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Right-hand wah-wah scratching with muted strings to a drum beat
10 mins: Slow transition between open E bass notes and the E7#9 chord voicing
15 mins: Practicing the main riff with the signature 3rd fret microtonal blues curl
15 mins: 12th-position E blues scale bends and vibrato drills with metronome
focusAreas: Rhythmic pocket and laid-back groove feel
Clean separation between low E pedal bass and upper chord stabs
Accurate pitch control on aggressive high-string bends
Dynamic expression using guitar volume and pick velocity
metronomeWork: Start with metronome clicking on beats 2 and 4 at 70 BPM to build groove independence
Gradually increase tempo to recording speed of 84 BPM
Practice intro rakes at 60 BPM ensuring even 16th-note subdivision

metadata.learningValue: The ultimate masterclass in wah-pedal rhythm, aggressive blues phrasing, and iconic thumb-over chord voicings.
